title: Capacity fallthrough scenarios and canary latency benchmarks for Dedicated Autoscale
creator: Avery Chen
description: Goal: Define a concise quarterly plan to validate fallthrough behaviors for Dedicated capacity (when primary pool is exhausted) and to establish canary latency/throughput benchmarks that will guide autoscaler decision thresholds. Scope: 1) Enumerate realistic fallthrough scenarios (regional depletion, scheduled maintenance, sudden burst beyond pool quota). 2) Design canary tests that exercise end-to-end stack (routing -> model variant fallback -> KV cache warmup) at production-like QPS. 3) Produce SLO/alert tuning guidance and rollout gating for Dedicated customers. Deliverables: - Scenario catalog with expected frequency and priority. - Canary test harness in CI and a lightweight harness for manual replay. - Benchmark dataset and dashboards (console route + token-level breakdown). - A short operational playbook for on-call and capacity ops to follow during incidents. Links: Confluence doc (design): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Capacity+Fallthrough+and+Canary+Plan; Example PR for harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4872; Dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/CPUYd4k/canary-latency
acceptance_criteria: A catalog of at least 4 prioritized fallthrough scenarios with expected probability buckets and mitigation notes
Canary harness that can be triggered from CI and produces stable latency/throughput metrics within 15% variance across 3 runs
Dashboards ingesting canary telemetry with token-level cost and latency breakdowns
Playbook with run/rollback steps and a list of alert thresholds that map to specific operational actions
